paragraphs: This paper presents a gravimetric method for estimating progress of CO2-evolving decarboxylation from initial and subsequent gross-mass readings. Observed loss is normalized against either a stoichiometric CO2 capacity or an empirically defined reference endpoint. The derivation concerns measurable mass transfer, not a particular route of reaction initiation. Developed through Decarboxulator since 2023, its principal worked applications concern thermal cannabinoid processing, lot calibration, readability, and scaled stopping targets.

The established manual thermal workflow is extended through two heater–balance load paths and a proposed continuous-acquisition controller. Complementary pressure-inventory calculations address gas retained in or vented from closed vessels. The stoichiometric and gravimetric framework also applies to characterized enzyme-catalyzed decarboxylations, provided dissolved carbon, gas escape, and competing mass transfers are considered. Existing calculations and procedures are distinguished from proposed instrumentation and experimental evaluation.
